Rashi on Gittin 71b:1:1.hebrew: שני אחין חרשים - כיון דהם חרשים, לא איכפת לן בנשותיהן אם הן אחת פקחות, דמ"מ הם לא כנסו אלא ברמיזה:
Rashi on Gittin 71b:1:1.english: Two deaf-mute brothers - Since they are deaf-mutes, we are not concerned about [the status of] their wives — whether they are [both] competent [or] one [is] competent [and one is a deaf-mute] — for in any case, they [the brothers] only married [them] through gesturing:

Rashi on Gittin 71b:1:2.hebrew: וכן שתי אחיות חרשות - לא איכפת לן בפקחות של בעלים, דהן לא נכנסו אלא ברמיזה; לפיכך פטורות מן החליצה, דיוצאה משום אחות אשה, דכל עריות פטורות מן החליצה:
Rashi on Gittin 71b:1:2.english: And similarly, two deaf-mute sisters - We are not concerned with the [halakhic] competence of the husbands, for they [the sisters] only entered [into marriage] through gesturing; therefore, they are exempt from chalitzah, for she is discharged on account of [being] a wife's sister, since all forbidden relatives [arayot] are exempt from chalitzah:

Rashi on Gittin 71b:2:1.hebrew: ואם היו נכריות - ומת אחד מהן, השני אינו יכול לחלוץ מפני שהוא חרש או שהיא חרשת ואינה יכולה לומר "מאן יבמי", אלא יכנסו:
Rashi on Gittin 71b:2:1.english: And if they were unrelated women - and one of them [the brothers] died, the second [brother] cannot perform chalitzah because he is a deaf-mute, or she is a deaf-mute and cannot say, "My brother-in-law refuses"; rather, they may marry [them in levirate marriage]:

Rashi on Gittin 71b:2:2.hebrew: ואם רצו להוציאן - אחרי כן יוציאו, דאתי גט חרש ומפקע זיקת קידושי חרש; אלמא היכא דנפלה ליה מאחיו חרש מפיק, ולא גזרינן אטו אחיו פקח:
Rashi on Gittin 71b:2:2.english: And if they wanted to divorce them - afterwards, they may divorce [them], for the bill of divorce of a deaf-mute comes and nullifies the levirate bond [created by] the betrothal of a deaf-mute; thus, where she fell to him [for levirate marriage] from his deaf-mute brother, he may divorce [her], and we do not make a decree on account of [the case of] his halakhically competent brother:

Rashi on Gittin 71b:3:1.english: As we initially answered - that she fell to him [for levirate marriage] from his halakhically competent brother:

Rashi on Gittin 71b:4:1.hebrew: חלוקין עליו חביריו - דאפי' פקח ונתחרש אינו יכול לגרש, ואפי' יודע לכתוב; ולא תימא רשב"ג מפרש מילתיה דתנא קמא, דהכי שמיע ליה לרבי יוחנן דמיפלג פליג:
Rashi on Gittin 71b:4:1.english: His colleagues disagree with him - [meaning] that even one who was of sound senses and [later] became a deaf-mute cannot divorce [his wife], and even [if] he knows how to write; and do not say [that] Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is [merely] explaining the statement of the Tanna Kamma, for thus did Rabbi Yochanan hear [by tradition], that he indeed disagrees:

Rashi on Gittin 71b:5:1.english: She became an imbecile - she [became so] after she was married:

Rashi on Gittin 71b:5:2.hebrew: לא יוציא - אסור להוציאה. ואע"פ שפקחת ונתחרשה יוציאה, דאשה לא בעינן דעתה, שהרי יוצאה לרצונה ושלא לרצונה; היכא דנשטת אמור רבנן "לא יוציא", דכיון שאינה יודעת לשמור עצמה ינהגו בה הפקר בזנות, וכן מפרש לקמן:
Rashi on Gittin 71b:5:2.english: He must not divorce [her] - It is forbidden [for him] to divorce her. Even though [if she was] of sound mind and became a deaf-mute he may divorce her — for [with respect to] a woman we do not require her consent, since she is divorced both with her consent and without her consent — [nevertheless,] where she became an imbecile the Rabbis said "he must not divorce [her]," because since she does not know how to guard herself, [people] will treat her as ownerless for licentiousness, and so it explains below:

Rashi on Gittin 71b:5:3.hebrew: ואע"ג דחריף - אבל מדבר מתוך הכתב, לא ממעט:
Rashi on Gittin 71b:5:3.english: And even though he is sharp - but one who communicates through writing, [the Mishnah] does not exclude:

Rashi on Gittin 71b:7:1.hebrew: אי נמי - האי "עולמית" לכדרבי יצחק אתא, למידק מינה מדקתני סיפא "עולמית" ורישא לא תנא "עולמית", משום דרישא דרבנן כדרבי יצחק, וסיפא דאורייתא, דגבי מגרש בעינן דעתו, שהאיש אינו מוציא אלא לרצונו:
Rashi on Gittin 71b:7:1.english: Alternatively - this [word] "ever" comes for [the teaching of] Rabbi Yitzchak: to infer from it — since the latter clause teaches "ever" and the first clause does not teach "ever" — that the first clause is rabbinic, in accordance with Rabbi Yitzchak, whereas the latter clause is [by] Torah law, for regarding the one who divorces we require his intent, as a man divorces only willingly:

Rashi on Gittin 71b:7:2.hebrew: אפיקחת בעל כרחה - מתגרשת, ואע"פ שלא מדעתה:
Rashi on Gittin 71b:7:2.english: [Like] a competent woman against her will - she is divorced even though [it is] without her consent:

Tosafot on Gittin 71b:7:1.hebrew: אי נמי לכדרבי יצחק - אביי נמי דייק "עולמית" לכדרבי יצחק בפרק חרש (יבמות קיג:), דקאמר התם: אף אנן נמי תנינא כדרבי יצחק, ודייק מדקתני "עולמית" גבי נשתטה, ולא תנא גבי נישטת היא; אלא דהכא דייק מדקתני "עולמית" אתרוייהו, אנתחרש ונשתטה — הא דקתני ליה אחרש אשמועינן אפי' יכול לדבר ע"י כתב, ואנשתטה לכדרבי יצחק. ורב פפא דחי, דמ"מ איכא למימר דלא אתא "עולמית" אלא לכדרבי יצחק גרידא:
Tosafot on Gittin 71b:7:1.english: Alternatively, in accordance with Rabbi Yitzḥak - Abaye also infers [the word] "never" [as coming] in accordance with Rabbi Yitzḥak in the chapter [entitled] Ḥeresh (Yevamot 113b), where he says there: "We too have also learned [in the Mishnah] in accordance with Rabbi Yitzḥak," and he infers [this] from the fact that [the Mishnah] teaches "never" regarding [where] he became an imbecile, and does not teach [it] regarding [where] she became an imbecile. Rather, [the difference is] that here [one] infers from the fact that it teaches "never" regarding both of them — regarding "he became a deaf-mute" and "he became an imbecile" — [that] that which it teaches regarding a deaf-mute teaches us [that he cannot divorce] even [if] he can speak through writing, and regarding "he became an imbecile," [it is] in accordance with Rabbi Yitzḥak. And Rav Pappa rejects [this], for in any event one can say that "never" comes only for Rabbi Yitzḥak's [teaching] alone:
